subject: TTFT pilot commitment checklist & chunking plan
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>

Cc: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: TTFT pilot commitment checklist & chunking plan

Thanks again for taking the call this morning — great to align on scope. Below is a concise recap and proposed next steps so we can lock in the pilot. Please call out anything I missed.

Recap (what we agreed on)
- Business goal: Reduce screen-to-first-interactive latency for chat flows in FinLytics mobile app; improve perceived responsiveness for conversational search.
- Pilot target: p95 time-to-first-token (TTFT) target and streaming expectations for an initial production-like pilot.

Performance targets we discussed (proposal)
- TTFT (p95): 200 ms end-to-end for 1–2KB prompt payloads (client -> Redwood -> model -> first token back).
- Throughput: sustain 100 req/s for peak traffic window with autoscaling planned for burst to 250 req/s.
- Concurrency: target 50 concurrent active streams in pilot region (US East).
- Streaming mode: SSE preferred for initial integration; websocket optional for later if you need bi-directional or lower head-of-line effects.
- Chunk cadence: target 200–400 ms cadence for incremental emits; allow final chunk flush to deliver remaining tokens.

Integration & operational items
- Tech follow-up: 60–90 minute engineering session (Dev + Oliver + Monica) to walk probe harness and sample payloads (action: schedule by Wed).
- Perf probe: Redwood will supply a perf-probe config and prebuilt harness for you to run locally against the pilot endpoint.
- Security/compliance: we'll send our standard pilot DPA + SOC 2 evidence packet; please share your security contact if not already included.
- SOW: attached draft SOW for the pilot (attachment). If SOW is ok we can start provision on Mon 19 Jul.

Immediate asks
1) Oliver — confirm p95 TTFT target (200 ms) is acceptable as baseline, or indicate if you need a tighter SLA (e.g., 150 ms) and which traffic slices are most critical.
2) Share sample payload sizes and typical prompt patterns (one-off, multi-turn with context).
3) Availability windows for the engineering deep-dive (Dev + FinLytics infra).

Attachments: finlytics-pilot-sow-draft.pdf, redwood-demo-clip-20270712.mp4

Thanks — I’ll coordinate the calendar after I hear back.

Thanks Karthik — helpful recap. A few notes and clarifications from our side after internal sync: 

- Target tweak: Our product lead is pushing for p95 TTFT = 150 ms for high-value search hits (we understand that this is aggressive). For the broader traffic set we can accept 200 ms. Can you comment on the delta and what changes (model size, quantization, prioritized routing) would be required to hit 150 ms?
- Streaming: SSE is fine for reads. For multi-turn chat where we may send incremental user edits from the client, we may need websocket later — but let's keep SSE for pilot to reduce client work.
- Chunk cadence: 200 ms cadence looks good; curious what the recommended smallest chunk size is to avoid excessive tokenization overhead.
- Security: cc’ing our infra lead Sara; she’ll share a security contact and the questions.

We are ok to review the SOW — will aim to get sign-off by EOD Thu if the numbers are aligned. Also can you share the perf-probe config so we can start internal testing?

Oliver

Subject: Re: TTFT pilot commitment checklist & chunking plan

Oliver — quick engineering readout on feasibility and recommended probe setup. TL;DR: 150 ms p95 is possible for some traffic slices with optimizations; pilot should validate with representative payloads.

Feasibility notes
- 200 ms p95 baseline: achievable using our standard optimized runtime (FP16 quantized medium model variant) with prefix caching and continuous batching tuned for 10–20 ms per-token kernel latency.
- 150 ms p95 for high-value hits: requires one or more of the following: smaller model variant for first-token priming, warm KV-cache (pin hot contexts), tighter concurrency isolation (dedicated slot for critical traffic), or regional proximity (edge / us-east availability zone). Expect cost to increase ~10–25% for aggressive priming.

Streaming & chunk cadence
- SSE is the simplest integration and avoids websocket connection management; it introduces some head-of-line risk for concurrent downstream messages but acceptable at low concurrency.
- Chunk cadence: aim for 200–350 ms cadence for initial pilot. Avoid sub-100 ms cadence — per-chunk overhead (network + framing + tokenization) can dominate.
- Minimum payload per chunk: target > 8–12 tokens to amortize overhead. If you need very fast first token, send a 1–2 token priming prefix to speed initial emit (we can coordinate prefix priming in the probe).

Probe & test harness
- I attached a reference perf-probe config (perf-probe-config.yaml) and a script to run 3 scenarios: baseline, primed-hot, and burst. Please run the probe from a machine in your us-east region and share raw logs.
- We recommend the following probe parameters: 1000 warmup requests, 5000 measured requests, concurrency sweep at [10, 25, 50, 100], sample payloads of 1KB / 2KB / 5KB.

Next steps (engineering)
1) Karthik: schedule a 60–90m technical session for Wed Jul 14 or Thu Jul 15 with FinLytics infra + app teams.
2) Oliver: share a representative set of 10 sample prompts (anonymized) and average payload sizes.
3) Sara: we’ll start a narrow security questionnaire exchange once we have your contact.

Attachment: perf-probe-config.yaml

Appreciate the quick responses — summary & commitments below so we can move to SOW sign and provisioning.

Agreed items
- Pilot scope: FinLytics will run a US East pilot with Redwood for 3 weeks.
- Performance targets:
  - Critical traffic slice: target p95 TTFT = 150 ms (experimentally validated with primed workflows).
  - Broader traffic: target p95 TTFT = 200 ms.
- Streaming mode: SSE for pilot; plan websocket evaluation post-pilot for multi-turn edit flows.
- Chunk cadence: target 200–350 ms; min chunk ~8 tokens.

Action items & owners
- FinLytics (Oliver): share 10 anonymized sample prompts and confirm pilot start date window (proposed Mon Jul 19).
- FinLytics (Sara): share security contact and questionnaire items.
- Redwood (Dev): send perf-probe config + short run instructions (done — attached).
- Redwood (Karthik): update SOW with the 150/200 p95 buckets and send for signature (DocuSign link included).

I’ve updated HubSpot (deal FL-2027-0712) with these commitments and attached the revised SOW in the DocuSign packet. If you’re happy, we’ll provision the pilot endpoint on Mon Jul 19 and set a kickoff for Tue Jul 20 (engineering deep-dive).

Thanks all — passing to Sara for security contact and Oliver for sample prompts.
